def: Repeating cycle where an AI observes the world, decides on actions, and executes them autonomously.
why: Foundation of next-generation AI systems that don't just respond but actively work on your behalf.
tie: Ties to Story #1 & #4: SMS agents and safety departures highlight how agentic systems are both increasingly powerful and increasingly controversial.

def: Training AI systems using a constitution (set of principles) rather than human feedback alone.
why: Offers scalable alignment: teach principles once, apply to infinite behaviors.
tie: Directly referenced in Story #1 (OpenAI departures) and Story #3 (Apple's tighter security).

def: Time delay between a request and a response; measured in milliseconds.
why: In AI agents, sub-50ms latency feels instant; 200ms+ feels like a lag. Critical for user experience.
tie: Story #2 (DGX Spark reduces API latency 10x) and Story #4 (SMS agents need sub-second response).

def: Permission that allows an app to read and write to all files on a user's device, including system files.
why: Powerful but dangerous; used by productivity apps and screen recorders. Easy to abuse.
tie: Story #3: Apple tightens Full Disk Access rules after Meta Muse (screen recording) controversy.

def: Releasing AI model parameters publicly so anyone can download, run, and fine-tune the model.
why: Democratizes AI but raises concerns about misuse, safety, and responsibility.
tie: Story #2 (NVIDIA DGX optimized for open-weights) and Story #1 (Meta's open approach contrasts with Anthropic).

def: AI assistant integrated into a physical device worn on the body (glasses, earbuds, rings).
why: Always-on, hands-free access. Raises privacy concerns but enables seamless interaction.
tie: Story #5: Meta's Muse pivots to Ray-Ban glasses; Apple Glasses rumored for 2027.

def: Process of ensuring an AI system's goals and behaviors match human intent and values.
why: Core unsolved problem in AI safety. Misaligned systems can cause harm at scale.
tie: Story #1: OpenAI safety researcher departure signals alignment tensions at leading labs.

def: Amount of work (requests, tokens, inferences) a system can process per unit time.
why: More throughput = lower cost per request. Critical for enterprise AI deployment.
tie: Story #2 (DGX Spark throughput for on-prem) and Story #4 (SMS agents scaling to 2B users).
